title: 1.1 What people look like
unit_title: People, family and habits
unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
goal: Say what a person looks like (tall, short, young, old, long hair, a beard) and find the person someone describes.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.1 Meet the People: He is a man. becomes He is an old man. It adds no new grammar relationship: be + a description (Luis is tall.), has + a feature (A1 3.12 has: Diego has a beard.) and a/an before a description (an old man).
prerequisite: A1 1.1 boy, girl, man, woman, he, she, is; 1.5 an; 1.9 Who…?; 3.12 has.
speaking_outcome: A breathy h in has and hair (not the Spanish j), the y sound that starts young, and an old with the n joined to old, inside the complete sentence. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 1.2 What people do
unit_title: People, family and habits
unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
goal: Say what a person does with he/she and the -s ending (Luis drinks coffee.), against I drink coffee. and A1's Luis is drinking coffee.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.2 People in Action: He is eating. becomes He eats fruit. The one new grammar relationship is he/she + verb + -s (A1 has it only for wants/needs), taught as the contrast I drink coffee. / Luis drinks coffee. and heard against A1's is ...-ing.
prerequisite: A1 1.2 eating, drinking, reading, writing; 1.9 Who…?; 2.9 books; 5.1 fruit; 5.3 coffee, drink; 7.7 read; A1+ 1.1 the cast.
speaking_outcome: A clear final s in drinks and eats (/s/) and in reads (/z/), and writes with a clean /ts/, inside the complete sentence. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 1.3 What they do

title: 1.5 Brothers and sisters
unit_title: People, family and habits
unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
goal: Ask How many brothers and sisters do you have?, answer with I have ..., and say who is older or younger (This is my older sister. Luis has a younger brother.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.5 Brothers, Sisters and Adults: brothers and sisters become a question. The one new grammar relationship is the question frame How many + family word + do you have?, built from A1's How many ...? (How many apples are there?) and Do you ...? (Do you work?), answered with A1's I have. Older and younger grow A1+ 1.1's old and young into family words, with A1 1.5's an before older (an older sister). Has returns with names (Ana has two sisters.).
prerequisite: A1 1.5 brother, sister, an; A1 Have and Has (I have, he/she has); A1 How Many? (How many apples are there?); A1 Do you ...? questions (Do you work?); A1 numbers; A1+ 1.1 old, young and the cast.
speaking_outcome: Ask How many brothers and sisters do you have? as one smooth question, and say older and younger clearly, with the -er ending. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 1.6 Always, usually, sometimes, never
unit_title: People, family and habits
unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
goal: Say how often your parents and grandparents do something, with always, usually, sometimes and never before the verb (My grandmother always drinks tea.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.6 Parents and Grandparents: the family words return with how often each person does something. The one new grammar relationship is the frequency word between the person and the verb (My grandmother always drinks tea.), on A1+ 1.2's he/she -s and 1.3's runs in the park.
prerequisite: A1 1.6 father, mother, grandfather, grandmother; A1 1.9 Who ...?; A1 2.1 park; A1 5 tea and coffee; A1 3.10 my; A1+ 1.2 drinks; A1+ 1.3 runs; A1+ 1.4 the grandparents.
speaking_outcome: Place the frequency word before the verb in one smooth sentence (My father sometimes runs in the park.), with a clear -s on the verb. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 1.8 What they don't do

title: 1.9 Does your family...?
unit_title: People, family and habits
unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
goal: Ask about someone's family with does and answer with a short answer (Does your grandmother drink tea? Yes, she does.), and ask where and who with does (Where does your aunt live? Who does your cousin live with?).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.9 Who Is He? Who Are They?: A1 asks who family members are (Who is he? He is the father.); A1+ 1.9 asks what they do and where they live, with does. The one new grammar relationship is the question with does + the base verb, and its short answer: Does your grandmother drink tea? Yes, she does. / No, he doesn't. Where does and Who does put a question word before it (Where does your aunt live? Who does your cousin live with?). After does the verb loses its -s, as after 1.8's doesn't.
prerequisite: A1 1.9 Who; A1 4.3 Where; A1 4.8 Do you...? and Yes, I do.; A1 5.3 drink and tea; A1 4.8 run; A1+ 1.4 aunt, uncle, cousin, lives in, with; A1+ 1.6 the grandparents' tea and coffee and the parents running in the park; A1+ 1.8 doesn't.
speaking_outcome: Ask with does and a falling-rising question tone, keep the verb without -s after does (Does she drink...?), and answer with a short answer that keeps the person (Yes, she does. / No, he doesn't.). Do not require native-like speed.

title: 1.10 What is its name?
unit_title: People, family and habits
unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
goal: Ask and say a pet's name with its (What is its name? Its name is Max.) and say what a pet does with its things (The dog plays with its ball.), next to his and her for people.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.10 Pets: A1 names four pets and says what each is doing (The dog is running.); A1+ 1.10 gives each pet a name and its own things. The one new grammar relationship is its, the possessive for an animal or a thing, next to A1's his and her for people: What is its name? Its name is Max. / His name is Luis. / The dog plays with its ball.
prerequisite: A1 1.10 dog, cat, bird, rabbit, pet; A1 3.1 What is your name? and name; A1 3.10 his and her; A1 3.12 have; A1 4.2 bed; A1 5.2-5.3 food and water; A1 7.13 ball; A1+ 1.2 drinks, eats; A1 4.8 play.
speaking_outcome: Say its with a short i and a clear final ts (its name), different from his (with h and a z sound); ask What is its name? with falling intonation. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 1.11 With him, with her, with them
unit_title: People, family and habits
unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
lesson_title: With him, with her, with them
sub_lesson_title: With him, with her, with them
goal: Say who people do things with, using him, her and them instead of the person (She cooks dinner with her husband. / She cooks dinner with him.), and answer Who does ... with?
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.11 Friends and People: A1 names a husband and wife, their son and daughter and a friend (The husband and the wife are talking.); A1+ 1.11 says who they do things with. The one new grammar relationship is the object pronoun after with: him, her and them replace the person (She cooks dinner with her husband. / She cooks dinner with him.), next to the subject pronouns he, she and they. Her is both the possessive (her friend) and the object (with her).
prerequisite: A1 1.11 husband, wife, son, daughter, friend; A1 1.4 children; A1 1.6 mother, father; A1 3.10 his and her; A1 7.6 play football; A1+ 1.2 reads and the he/she -s (cooks, plays); A1+ 1.4 with; A1+ 1.9 Who does ... with?
speaking_outcome: Say him, her and them clearly at the end of the sentence, linked to with (with him, with her, with them); the th of them is soft. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 1.13 ¡La fiesta de Ana!
unit_title: People, family and habits
unit_outcome: Describe people and family, say what people do every day and how often, and ask about other people’s habits.
goal: Help Ana start her family party: find the guests from descriptions and from what they do, find the pets and the people doing things together, find the truth in a negative clue, and answer Ana's friends aloud with does, where, who and its.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 1.13 ¡Todos a la celebración!: A1 closes Unit 1 by bringing the family to one celebration; A1+ 1.13 closes A1+ Unit 1 at Ana's family party with no new language. The learner finds guests from descriptions (1.1) and from the he/she -s (1.2-1.3), finds the pets with its (1.10) and the people doing things with him, her and them (1.11), uses a doesn't clue (1.8), and answers does, where and who questions and What is its name? aloud (1.4, 1.9, 1.10).
speaking_outcome: Answer four friends' questions aloud for Ana: a short answer with does, where her uncle lives, who her cousin lives with and the name of her rabbit.

title: 2.1 Where people go
unit_title: Places, things and how we describe them
unit_outcome: Say where people go and how they get there, talk about the things people have, point things out and compare them, put things in order, and ask about favorites.
goal: Say where people go with go to and goes to (I go to the gym. / Luis goes to the gym.), with three new places: gym, pool and office.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 2.1 Places Around Me: A1 names places (It is a park.) and says what people are doing in them (The girl is running in the park.); A1+ 2.1 says where people go. The one new grammar relationship is go to + place with he/she goes, the -es spelling of go, taught against the I-form (I go to the gym. / Luis goes to the gym.) and heard against A1's is going (Luis is going to the gym.). New places: gym, pool, office.
prerequisite: A1 2.1 places (park) and It is a/an; A1 4.6 go to school; A1 6.3 I am going to; A1 6.11 goes; A1+ 1.2-1.3 the he/she -s; A1+ 1.9 Where does…?; A1+ 1.3 Ana swims and Sofia runs in the park.
speaking_outcome: Say goes with a long o and a final z sound (/ɡoʊz/), different from go; keep to the in go to the gym short. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 2.2 How do you go there?
unit_title: Places, things and how we describe them
unit_outcome: Say where people go and how they get there, talk about the things people have, point things out and compare them, put things in order, and ask about favorites.
goal: Ask and say how people go to a place (How do you go to the pool? I go by bike. / How does Luis go to the gym? He goes by car.), with A1's bus, car and bike and walk.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 2.2 Streets and Transportation: A1 names the street, the bridge, the bus, the car and the bike (It is a bus.); A1+ 2.2 asks how people go somewhere. The one new grammar relationship is the question How + do/does + go to …?, built from A1 4.8's Do you…? and A1+ 1.9's Does…?, answered with A1 6.2's by bus / by bike and walk (How do you go to the pool? I go by bike. / How does Luis go to the gym? He goes by car.). The people and places are 2.1's.
prerequisite: A1 2.2 bus, car, bike; A1 6.2 by and walk; A1 4.8 Do you…?; A1+ 1.9 Does…? and Where does…?; A1+ 1.7 How often…?; A1+ 2.1 go to / goes to, gym, pool, office.
speaking_outcome: Ask How do you go…? and How does Luis go…? with falling intonation, the do/does short and weak; answer with by linked to the vehicle (by bike). Do not require native-like speed.

title: 2.4 What's this?
unit_title: Places, things and how we describe them
unit_outcome: Say where people go and how they get there, talk about the things people have, point things out and compare them, put things in order, and ask about favorites.
goal: Ask and answer What's this? with the short forms What's, It's and isn't (What's this? It's a wallet. / It isn't a phone. It's a camera.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 2.4 What Is It?: A1 asks and answers with full forms (What is it? It is a book.); A1+ 2.4 uses the short forms people say. The one new grammar relationship is the contraction of is in What's and It's, and of is not in isn't, taught against the full forms (It is a watch. / It's a watch.) and joined to A1 2.2's negative contrast (It isn't a phone. It's a camera.). The things are A1 2.3's and A1+ 2.3's.
prerequisite: A1 2.2 It is a…, not a…; A1 2.3 book, pen, phone, bag; A1 2.4 What is it?; A1 2.5 this; A1 4.2 Is it…?; A1+ 2.3 watch, wallet, camera.
speaking_outcome: Say It's as one syllable with a clear final ts, What's with a final ts, and isn't as IZ-nt with no vowel between z and n. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 2.5 This one, but that one
unit_title: Places, things and how we describe them
unit_outcome: Say where people go and how they get there, talk about the things people have, point things out and compare them, put things in order, and ask about favorites.
goal: Contrast a near thing and a far one with but (This bag is red, but that bag is blue.) and say this one and that one instead of repeating the thing (This one is red, but that one is blue.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 2.5 This and That: A1 says This is a phone. for a near thing and That is a phone. for a far one; A1+ 2.5 sets the two against each other in one sentence. The one new grammar relationship is but joining two taught clauses (This bag is red, but that bag is blue.), with this one and that one standing for the thing (A1 2.10's Which one? The red one.): This one is red, but that one is blue. Each scene has two photos from the same camera behind the speaker: in the first the speaker looks down at the near thing and touches it (this), in the second the speaker faces the far thing and points down at it (that). A but sentence plays as two turns, so the picture switches on but. Two scenes are also photographed with the colors swapped, so a picture card tells this from that, not the color alone.
prerequisite: A1 2.5 this and that; A1 2.8 colors; A1 2.10 Which one? The red one.; A1 3.12 This car is mine. (this + noun); A1 2.3 bag, chair; A1 2.2 bike; A1+ 1.5 Do you have…?
speaking_outcome: Say but short and weak (/bət/) with a small pause before it; stress the two colors (This one is RED, but that one is BLUE). Say this with a short i and that with an open a. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 2.8 My favorite color
unit_title: Places, things and how we describe them
unit_outcome: Say where people go and how they get there, talk about the things people have, point things out and compare them, put things in order, and ask about favorites.
goal: Ask and say favorite colors (What's your favorite color? My favorite color is purple. / Her favorite color is pink.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 2.8 Basic Colors: A1 names colors (It is red.); A1+ 2.8 asks and says which color someone likes most, with favorite after my, his and her (My favorite color is purple. / His favorite color is green.) and the question What's your favorite color?, with A1+ 2.4's What's. Each cast member paints a wall of their home in their favorite color: Ana purple, Luis yellow, Sofia pink, Diego green. Listen brings back 2.4's short forms (Is your favorite color blue? title: 2.11 Taller than Sofia
unit_title: Places, things and how we describe them
unit_outcome: Say where people go and how they get there, talk about the things people have, point things out and compare them, put things in order, and ask about favorites.
goal: Compare two people or two things with -er than (Luis is taller than Sofia. / The bus is bigger than the car. / I am older than my brother.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 2.11 Big and Small: A1 says It is a big dog. / It is a small dog. about one thing at a time; A1+ 2.11 compares two in one photo with the -er form and than (The brown dog is bigger than the white dog.). big doubles its g (bigger). It brings back A1+ 1.1's tall, short, old and young and 1.5's older and younger, now with than (My brother is older than me.). Two people or two things share each photo: Sofia beside Luis (1.1), Luis with his older and his younger brother (1.5), a bus beside a car, a big brown dog beside a small white dog, and a grandfather beside a boy on a bench.
prerequisite: A1 2.11 big, small; A1+ 1.1 tall, short, old, young; A1+ 1.5 older, younger, my brother; A1 2.2 bus, car; A1 1.10 dog; A1 brown, white; A1+ 2.10 the brown one; A1 2.12 or.
speaking_outcome: Say than with a soft th and a weak vowel (thən), linked to the comparative (TALLer than). Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.1 Nice to meet you
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Introduce a friend (This is my friend Luis.) and answer an introduction (Nice to meet you. / Nice to meet you, too.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.1 Greetings and Names: A1 greets people and asks and gives a name (Hello. What is your name? My name is Ana.); A1+ 3.1 introduces one person to another. It adds no new grammar relationship: This is + my friend + a name presents a person (A1 2.5's This is for a thing, A1 1.11's friend), and the fixed replies Nice to meet you. and Nice to meet you, too. answer it. Sofia and Luis introduce each other to a newcomer in a café, and Ana and Diego meet him there.
prerequisite: A1 3.1 hello, goodbye, good morning and What is your name? My name is …; A1 2.5 This is …; A1 1.11 friend; A1 4.10 night, A1 4.11 see and A1 4.12 tomorrow; A1+ 2.4 What's; A1+ 2.1 goes to the gym/pool/office/park.
speaking_outcome: Say Nice to meet you as one phrase, meet and you joined (MEET-choo is fine), and too with a long u; stress friend and the name in This is my friend Luis. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.2 I'm, you're, we're
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Use the short forms I'm, you're and we're (I'm at the gym. / You're tall. / We're in the park.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.2 I, You, and We: A1 says I am, you are and we are; A1+ 3.2 uses the short forms people say. The one new grammar relationship is the contraction of am and are after I, you and we (I'm, you're, we're), taught against the full forms (I am at the gym. / I'm at the gym.). Speaker perspective stays explicit: a person alone says I'm, two people together say we're, and you're is said to the other person in the photo (Sofia and Luis back to back: You're tall. / I'm short.).
prerequisite: A1 3.2 I am, you are, we are; A1 4.3 in; A1 4.10 at; A1 1.11 friends; A1+ 1.1 tall and short; A1+ 2.1 the gym, the pool, the office and the park, and go to.
speaking_outcome: Say I'm as one syllable ending in m, you're like your, and we're like weer; never add a vowel between the pronoun and the short form. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.3 He's, she's, they're
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Say what people are doing with the short forms he's, she's and they're (He's drinking coffee. / They're running.), and ask What's she doing?
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.3 Am, Is, and Are: A1 asks What is she doing? and answers She is reading. with the full forms; A1+ 3.3 uses the short forms. The one new grammar relationship is the contraction of is and are after he, she and they with -ing (He's drinking coffee. / They're running.), taught against the full forms, with A1+ 2.4's What's in the question (What's she doing?). Listen sets it against A1+ 1.2's habit (He drinks coffee.). The short form he's is is, never a possessive.
prerequisite: A1 3.3 What is she doing? She is …-ing; A1 1.2 the -ing actions; A1 7.6 watch TV and ride a bike; A1 4.12 now; A1+ 1.2 drinks, reads; A1+ 2.4 What's; A1+ 3.2 I'm, you're, we're.
speaking_outcome: Say he's and she's with a final z sound (heez, sheez) and they're like there; keep the -ing clear. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.4 No, I'm not.
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Answer yes/no questions with the negative short forms (No, I'm not. / No, she isn't. / No, they aren't.) and say what is true instead (They aren't swimming. They're running.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.4 Yes and No: A1 answers Is he …? / Are you …? with Yes, he is. / No, she is not.; A1+ 3.4 answers with the negative short forms. The one new grammar relationship is the contraction of am not and are not (I'm not, aren't), next to A1+ 2.4's isn't, in short answers (No, I'm not. / No, they aren't.) and in a denial followed by what is true (They aren't swimming. They're running.). A short answer keeps the person of the question.
prerequisite: A1 3.4 yes/no questions with be; A1+ 2.4 isn't; A1+ 3.2 I'm, you're, we're; A1+ 3.3 he's, she's, they're; A1+ 1.1 short; A1+ 2.1 the gym, the office and the pool.
speaking_outcome: Say aren't as one syllable, AHRNT, with the final t; say I'm not with the m and n joined. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.5 Three years older
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Say how much older or younger someone is (She's three years older than him. / He's three years younger than her.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.5 Ages 11-15: A1 asks How old are you? and answers with a number of years old; A1+ 3.5 compares two ages. The one new grammar relationship is a number of years before A1+ 2.11's comparative (She's three years older than him. / He's three years younger than her.), taught against the comparative alone (She's older than him.). Each photo shows a sister and a brother, each behind a birthday cake with number candles, so the difference can be counted. The pronoun after than is A1+ 1.11's him or her.
prerequisite: A1 3.5 How old …? and eleven to fifteen; A1 2.6 two to four; A1+ 1.5 older and younger; A1+ 1.11 him and her; A1+ 2.11 older than and younger than; A1+ 3.3 he's and she's.
speaking_outcome: Say years with a clear y and a final z sound; keep older than and younger than as one group, with than unstressed. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.6 Both the same age
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Say that two people are twins, are the same age, or are both sixteen (They're both sixteen.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.6 Ages 16-20: A1 asks How old is she? and answers with one age; A1+ 3.6 says what two ages have in common. It adds no new grammar relationship: both goes between they're and the age (They're both sixteen.), the same age follows they're as a description (They're the same age.), and twins is a noun after they're. Two pairs of twins and two other pairs sit behind birthday cakes with number candles from A1 3.6's range, so the ages can be read; twins and the same age are told apart in text, because a picture cannot show who is a twin. 3.4's aren't and 3.5's years older come back (They aren't the same age. She's two years older than him.).
prerequisite: A1 3.6 sixteen to twenty and How old …?; A1+ 1.5 older; A1+ 3.3 they're; A1+ 3.4 aren't; A1+ 3.5 years older than.
speaking_outcome: Say both with a long o and a soft th at the end; say the same age as one group. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.7 What language do you speak?
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Ask and say which languages people speak (What language do you speak? I speak Spanish and English.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.7 Where Are You From?: A1 asks where people are from (Where are you from? I am from Mexico.); A1+ 3.7 asks what language they speak. It adds no new grammar relationship: What + language opens A1 4.8's do you question (What language do you speak?), and speak takes A1+ 1.2's -s (Diego speaks Spanish.). Spanish, the A1 nationality, is also the language. A1 3.7-3.8's country photos, with their flags, show where people speak Spanish or English; the cast's languages follow their A1 countries (Ana Mexican, Luis American, Sofia Canadian, Diego Spanish) and are always said, never guessed from a picture. The 3.1 newcomer asks Ana and Diego.
prerequisite: A1 3.7-3.8 countries and nationalities; A1 4.8 Do you …?; A1 1.11 people; A1+ 1.2 the he/she -s; A1+ 3.1 the café newcomer; A1+ 3.2 we.
speaking_outcome: Say speak with a long ee and English as ING-glish, two syllables. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.8 A Canadian nurse
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Put a nationality before a noun, with a or an and never with -s (Sofia is a Canadian nurse. / Luis is an American driver. / They're two Spanish men.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.8 Canada and Spain: A1 says a nationality after be (I am Canadian.); A1+ 3.8 puts the nationality before a noun (a Canadian nurse). The one new grammar relationship is that word order, with an before American, and an adjective that never takes -s when its noun does (two Spanish men, never Spanishes). The cast's nationalities are A1's (Ana Mexican, Sofia Canadian, Luis American, Diego Spanish); the new work photos show Ana teaching, Sofia nursing and Luis driving a bus, and 1.5's photo of Diego and his brother in Spain. Picture banks change the job or the people; nationality is told apart in Listen.
prerequisite: A1 3.7-3.8 nationalities; A1 3.9 teacher, nurse, driver; A1 2.6 two; A1+ 1.5 brothers; A1+ 2.9 men and women; A1+ 3.2 I'm, we're; A1+ 3.3 they're.
speaking_outcome: Say an American as one group (a-nAmerican); stress the noun after the nationality. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.9 What do you do?
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Ask about someone's work with What do you do? / What does she do? and answer with a job and where people work (She's a nurse. She works in a hospital.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.9 Professions: A1 asks What is your job? and answers I am a teacher.; A1+ 3.9 asks the way people usually do. The one new grammar relationship is What + do/does + subject + do? (What do you do? / What does Ana do?), answered with a job (She's a teacher.) or with works in + a place (She works in a hospital.). Ana is a teacher in a school, Sofia a nurse in a hospital, Luis drives a bus and Diego works in an office (A1+ 2.1).
prerequisite: A1 3.9 jobs and What is your job?; A1 2.1 school and hospital; A1 4.8 do; A1+ 1.7 works; A1+ 1.9 Does…?; A1+ 2.1 the office; A1+ 3.3 he's and she's.
speaking_outcome: In What do you do? the second do is stressed; in What does she do? keep does short (duz). Do not require native-like speed.

grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.13 Phone Number and Address: A1 answers What is your address? with It is 12 Park Street.; A1+ 3.13 says where people live. The one new grammar relationship is lives at + house number + street (She lives at eighteen Park Street.), taught against lives on + street alone (He lives on Park Street.) and A1+ 2.7's lives on + floor, with in + a house or an apartment; neighbor is the one new noun. The cast live on floors 6 to 9 of one building (A1+ 2.6-2.7), so Diego is Ana's neighbor, and its gym, store, restaurant, pool and office come back on their floors. title: 3.14 I want to be an artist
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
lesson_title: I want to be an artist
sub_lesson_title: I want to be an artist
goal: Say what people want to be with want to be + a job (She wants to be a singer. / What do you want to be? I want to be an artist.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.14 More Jobs: A1 says what someone's job is (He is a singer.); A1+ 3.14 says what someone wants to be. The one new grammar relationship is want(s) + to be + a/an + job (She wants to be a singer.), set against is + a job (She's a singer.) and against isn't (She isn't a doctor. She wants to be a doctor.); the question is What do you want to be? / What does she want to be?. Children play at A1's jobs in five new photos, Diego paints at home (he works in an office, 3.9), and in Ana's classroom 2.12's Stand up and Sit down come back with the question.
prerequisite: A1 3.14 jobs; A1 4.5 want; A1+ 2.12 Stand up and Sit down; A1+ 3.4 isn't; A1+ 3.9 What do you do?
speaking_outcome: Join want to be (WAN-tuh-bee); stress the job. Do not require native-like speed.

title: 3.15 Review: new people, new homes
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Review every A1+ Unit 3 step with new people: introductions, short forms of be, short answers, ages, both, languages and nationalities, jobs, hair, 's, whose and hers, addresses with at, and want to be, with no new language.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.15 Unit 3 Review: A1 reviews Unit 3 with fresh scenes; A1+ 3.15 reviews every A1+ Unit 3 step with ten fresh photos of new people and no new language: This is my … and Nice to meet you (3.1), she's, he's and they're with -ing (3.2-3.3), No, he isn't (3.4), three years older than (3.5), twins and both (3.6), a Spanish cook who speaks Spanish (3.7-3.8), What does he do? and works in (3.9), his hair is long (3.10), the man's camera (3.11), Whose …? and hers (3.12), lives at eleven Park Street (3.13) and wants to be a farmer (3.14). 2.5's but, 2.11's shorter and 2.12's Stand up and Sit down come back. Nobody in the photos speaks in the first person (the cast's voices belong to the cast), so the teacher asks and the co-teacher answers; nationality and language are said, never read from a picture.
speaking_outcome: Introduce and describe new people, say how old they are, what they do and want to be, whose things are and where they live, with every Unit 3 form, at a natural pace.

title: 3.16 La cena de los vecinos
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Help Ana run her building's international dinner: find the neighbors by job, by what they are doing, by their hair and by whose things they hold, find what each child wants to be and each country's food, and answer Ana's friends aloud about a guest's job, a guest's languages, Diego's brother and Sofia's bag.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.16 Cenas cruzadas: A1 closes Unit 3 at the community center's international dinner; A1+ 3.16 closes A1+ Unit 3 at the international dinner of Ana's building (the cast live on its floors 6 to 9, A1+ 2.7 and 3.13) with no new language. The learner finds the neighbors by job with a nationality before it (3.8), by what they are doing (3.3), by her or his hair (3.10) and by whose things they hold (3.11-3.12), finds what each child wants to be (3.14) and each country's food from an isn't clue (3.4, 3.8), and answers What does she do?, What language does he speak?, Diego's introduction of his brother and Is this your bag? aloud for Ana (3.9, 3.7, 3.1, 3.4 and 3.11).
speaking_outcome: Answer four friends aloud for Ana: what a guest does, which languages another guest speaks, a greeting for Diego's brother and whose bag Luis has found.

prerequisite: A1 5.1 fruit, apples, oranges, strawberries, bananas; A1 3.12 has; A1 5.4 How many … are there?; A1+ 1.2 eats.
speaking_outcome: Join a lot of into one phrase (a-LOT-of, of very short) and stress few in a few; do not require native-like speed.

title: 5.3 Would you like some tea?
unit_title: Food, drinks and shopping
unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
goal: Offer a drink with Would you like some …? and accept or refuse it (Yes, please. / No, thank you.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.3 Drinks: A1 names drinks and says who drinks them, and A1 5.10 answers an offer with Yes, please. / No, thank you.; A1+ 5.3 makes the offer: Would you like some + a drink? It is one new frame, learnt as a whole (would is not taken apart), with A1+ 4.15's some; hot chocolate is the one new drink. In each photo a host holds out a drink and the guest takes it or holds up a hand, so the photo shows the reply. The asker's voice always differs from the answerer's (Ana and Sofia share one voice, as do Luis and Diego). I'd like waits for 5.9.
prerequisite: A1 5.3 tea, coffee, juice, water; A1 5.10 Yes, please. / No, thank you.; A1+ 4.15 some; A1 5.5 I like.
speaking_outcome: Say Would you like as one phrase (WOOD-ja-LIKE is fine) with rising intonation at the end of the offer; do not require native-like speed.

title: 5.4 How much milk is there?

prerequisite: A1 5.4 How many … are there?; A1+ 5.1 a lot of, a few; A1+ 5.2 a little; A1+ 4.4 Is there…?, there isn't; A1 5.3 milk, juice.
speaking_outcome: Say How much milk with the stress on much and milk; join isn't much (IS-nt-MUCH); do not require native-like speed.

title: 5.7 Before dinner, after dinner
unit_title: Food, drinks and shopping
unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
goal: Say what you do before or after a meal (Ana washes her hands before dinner. / I drink coffee after breakfast.) and ask What do you do after dinner?
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.7 Meals: A1 says what I eat for breakfast, lunch and dinner and at what time; A1+ 5.7 places an action before or after a meal (Ana washes her hands before dinner. / Luis cleans the table after dinner.), with A1+ 1.2's he/she -s and the I-form. This is the before/after topic that left A1+ Unit 1 for A1 5.7 (2026-11-09); four of its 2026-10-31 dinner photos come back. A photo can show a meal waiting (a full plate) or finished (an empty plate), so only those photos set before against after; otherwise before and after are told apart by ear. A1+ 4.7's past comes back with cooked (Luis cooked dinner yesterday.). No clock times.
prerequisite: A1 5.7 breakfast, lunch, dinner, for lunch; A1+ 1.2 he/she -s; A1 4.7 clean; A1+ 4.5 washes; A1+ 4.7 -ed and yesterday; A1+ 1.7 What do you do …? frames.
speaking_outcome: Stress the meal after before and after (before DINner, after BREAKfast); do not require native-like speed.

title: 5.8 How much are the apples?

title: 5.9 I'd like a sandwich, please
unit_title: Food, drinks and shopping
unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.

speaking_outcome: Say I'd like as one word-group (IDE-like), with the d short; do not require native-like speed.

title: 5.10 Anything else?
unit_title: Food, drinks and shopping
unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
goal: Understand the seller's Anything else? and answer it: ask for one more thing (Yes, I'd like some bananas, please.) or finish (No, that's all, thank you.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.10 Ordering Politely 2: At the Market and Shops: A1 asks for things with quantities and accepts or declines an offer; A1+ 5.10 keeps a purchase going or ends it. At the market stall Luis points at bananas and Diego at apples, Ana waves with a full bag; at the café (5.9) Ana and Sofia finish their order. The seller is never pictured; a narrator in a voice other than the customer's asks.

title: 5.11 The red bag is cheaper
unit_title: Food, drinks and shopping
unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
goal: Compare prices with cheaper than and more expensive than (The red bag is cheaper than the black bag. / The black watch is more expensive than the blue watch.) and answer Which bag is cheaper? The red one.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.11 Buying Things: A1 says a thing is cheap or expensive; A1+ 5.11 compares two prices with A1+ 2.11's than: a short adjective takes -er (cheaper), and a long one takes more (more expensive), the one new relationship. Each photo shows two things of one kind side by side with their price cards, so every comparison is true of one photo only; a bank never offers the converse sentence that is also true (The black bag is more expensive than the red bag.). Which … is cheaper? is answered with A1+ 2.10's one. 5.6's want to comes back.
prerequisite: A1 5.11 cheap, expensive, buy; A1+ 2.11 -er than; A1+ 2.10 Which …? The red one.; A1 5.12 the tens; A1+ 5.6 want to.
speaking_outcome: Say more expensive as one group with the stress on PEN (more ex-PEN-sive) and cheaper with CHEAP; do not require native-like speed.

title: 5.12 Forty-five dollars
unit_title: Food, drinks and shopping
unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
goal: Say and understand prices and ages from twenty-one to ninety-nine (The shoes are forty-five dollars. / She's seventy-four.), and tell forty-five from fifty-four.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.12 Numbers 30 to 100: A1 says the tens from thirty to one hundred; A1+ 5.12 joins a ten and a unit with a hyphen (forty-five = forty + five), the numbers kept out of A1+ since Unit 2 (house numbers stayed at twenty or round tens). Four numbers are taught as items and the others are practised with the same rule. Banks set a number against the one with its digits swapped (forty-five / fifty-four). Each photo shows one thing behind its price card, or a grandparent behind a cake with two number candles; 5.8's How much is/are …? asks and 5.11's cheaper than returns.
prerequisite: A1 5.12 thirty to ninety; A1 numbers one to nine; A1+ 5.8 How much are …? They're …; A1+ 3.5 How old …?; A1+ 5.11 cheaper than.
speaking_outcome: Stress the ten and keep the unit clear (FOR-ty FIVE); keep the -ty of forty short so it is not heard as fourteen; do not require native-like speed.

lesson_title: Can you pass the salt, please?

goal: Ask someone at the table to pass something (Can you pass the salt, please? Here you are.) and ask for or offer a piece of cake.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.14 At the Table: A1 names things at the table (salt, sugar, cup, glass, bottle, plate, cake) and says what a cup or a glass holds (a cup of tea); A1+ 5.14 asks for something at the table with Can you pass the …, please?, a request answered by A1 5.9's Here you are., and adds a piece of for part of a cake, next to 5.3's Would you like …? and 5.9's I'd like …. prerequisite: A1 5.14 salt, sugar, cake, of; A1 5.9 Here you are.; A1 5.2-5.3 bread, water; A1+ 5.3 Would you like …?; A1+ 5.9 I'd like ….
speaking_outcome: Join Can you pass as one group (kn-you-PASS) and say a piece of with of short (a-PEE-suv); do not require native-like speed.

title: 5.16 Un sábado de compras
unit_title: Food, drinks and shopping
unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
goal: Spend Saturday with Ana and Luis at the market, a shop and a café: find shoppers by how much fruit they have, things by their price, the cheaper and the more expensive bag and watch, what café customers want, how much food is on each plate and what is in each dish, and answer aloud for Ana: agree, refuse an offer, finish shopping and say a price.
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.16 Un día en el mercado y el café: A1 closes Unit 5 with market purchases and a café order; A1+ 5.16 closes A1+ Unit 5 with Ana and Luis's Saturday at the market, a shop and a café, with no new language. The learner finds shoppers by a lot of / a few (5.1), things by their price (5.12), the cheaper and the more expensive bag and watch (5.11), what café customers want to do (5.6), how much rice or pasta is on each plate (5.1-5.2) and what is in each dish (5.13), then answers aloud for Ana with So do I. (5.5), No, thank you. to an offer (5.3), That's all (5.10) and They're three dollars. (5.8). Every mission photo is new and used only here.
speaking_outcome: Answer four times aloud for Ana: agree with Luis, refuse his offer politely, finish shopping and tell Diego the price of the apples.
